designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, even-weight icon grid with consistent strokes and condensed labels: it prints well in one ink on black with no fine detail to fill in, and the joke reads at a glance from 3 m. Weak spots: the bottom row of labels (HIGH BEAM / LAMP FAILURE) almost touches PROBABLY FINE, the two traction-control waves cross into a knot, and about 15% of the canvas below the headline is empty, so the print sits high.
designs.fix: Open up 40-60 px between the last label row and PROBABLY FINE, untangle the traction-control waves into two parallel lines, and crop the empty band at the bottom so the block centers properly on the back.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The four repeated 'Turn around.' steps are a real joke, and the loose brush dogs feel hand-made and warm. The line weight (around 8-12 px at full size) holds up for a single-ink print, and the serif title and italic captions belong together. On the tee the whole thing gets small and grey, though: the captions sit tight under the drawings, the crescent moon is a weak little mark, and the step-3/4 dogs are anatomically wobbly next to the confident step-6/7 curls.
designs.fix: Print it larger (or tighten the grid so the art fills more of the width), and give each caption about 30 px more air from its drawing so the steps read as a sequence from a distance.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: The linework is the most polished of the three: bold contours, tabby stripes that will hold in one ink, and a good break-out bed in panel 3. But the payoff caption BOX NOT SOLD SEPARATELY is tiny next to the art, so the joke barely reads on the shirt. In panel 3 the box wall lands right on top of the frame line on the left, and a stray double ledge line sits behind the bed. The bottom third of the canvas is empty, and cat-ignores-bed-sits-in-box is a well-worn gag.
designs.fix: Make BOX NOT SOLD SEPARATELY at least 2-3x bigger as a real headline under the panels, and fix the panel-3 spots where box and frame lines sit on top of each other (pull the box inside the frame or break the frame cleanly around it).
